pages.text:
• Quiet room (no talking by patient or observer)
• No smoking, caffeine, or exercise for ≥30 min before
No talking during rest period measurement
and between measurements • Empty bladder
• Note the time of most recent BP medication taken before
Cuff to fit arm size measurements
(small, usual, large1) • Relax for >5 min
• At first visit, record BP in both arms. Use the arm that
Arm bare and resting. gives the higher reading for subsequent readings
Mid-arm at midpoint of the sternum • Separate repeated measurements by 1–2 minutes
• Use an average of ≥2 readings obtained on ≥2 occasions
• Provide patients with the SBP/DBP readings verbally and
in writing

or manual auscultatory

periodically 1Use the correct cuff size, such that the bladder encircles
80% of the arm, and note if a larger- or smaller-than-normal
cuff size is used
2See validated electronic devices lists at www.stridebp.org
3For auscultatory readings, either the stethoscope
diaphragm or bell may be used. Use a palpated radial pulse
Feet flat on floor obliteration pressure to estimate SBP, then inflate the cuff
20–30 mm Hg above this level for auscultatory
determination of BP level. Deflate the cuff pressure 2 mm Hg
per second, and listen for Korotkoff sounds
